Gen. Kevin Admiral Nominated to Lead US Army Europe & Africa The Pentagon announced that President Trump has nominated Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral to serve as the next commanding general of the U.S. Army Europe and Africa. President Trump has nominated an Army lieutenant general to lead U.S. Army Europe and Africa The nominee currently serves as commanding general of III Corps and Fort Hood in Texas The Potomac Officers Club’s DOW summits will explore AI, network modernization and more The Pentagon announced that President Donald Trump has nominated Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral to serve as the next commanding general of the U.S. Army Europe and Africa . Table of Contents You might also like Lt. Gen. Douglas Schiess Confirmed as Chief of Space Operations Pete Small Named Acting NAVSEA Commander After Downey Retirement Pentagon Seeks Industry Feedback on Contract Accounting Reforms If confirmed, Admiral would also serve as commander of NATO’s Allied Land Command in Germany, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, a two-time Wash100 awardee, announced Thursday. Don’t miss the Potomac Officers Club’s 2026 Air and Space Summit happening this Thursday. Sign up now to join senior military and industry leaders as they discuss AI, commercial space relay, interoperable optical networks, Golden Dome and other modernization priorities. You can also register today for the 2026 Navy Summit on Aug. 27. This POC-hosted event will explore AI, digital engineering, autonomous platforms and other priorities shaping the future of naval readiness. Why Is the Army Europe & Africa Command Position Open? Defense News reported that Maj. Gen. Christopher Norrie has been serving as acting commander of Army Europe and Africa since Gen. Christopher Donahue stepped down from the position earlier this month, only 18 months into the role. Admiral, who leads III Corps and Fort Hood in Texas, is positioned to take over the post on a permanent basis pending confirmation. Who Is Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral? Admiral is a U.S. Army lieutenant general who currently serves as commanding general of III Corps and Fort Hood in Texas, a post he has held since August 2024. He previously served as commanding general of the 1st Cavalry Division at Fort Cavazos, Texas, and in Poland, from July 2023 to August 2024. Before that, he served as director of force management within the Office of the Deputy Chief of Staff, G-3/5/7, for the Army in Washington, D.C., from June 2021 to June 2023. Admiral was promoted to lieutenant general in August 2024. He earned his second star as a major general in August 2022 and his first star as a brigadier general in December 2019. https://www.dailyliberal.com.au/story/93.text: Russia has launched an intense barrage of ballistic missiles and drones, killing at least nine people and wounding 30 civilians in the Ukrainian capital. The overnight strikes follow a major Russian attack two days earlier that killed at least 10 people and wounded more than 50 others across Ukraine, as Moscow apparently looks to exploit Kyiv's critical shortage of Western-supplied anti-ballistic missile defences. The relentless cycle of attacks dims the potential of reaching a diplomatic end to Russia's more than four-year-old invasion of its neighbour. Russia's defence ministry said on Saturday it had launched a "massive strike" against "Ukrainian military-industrial complex facilities and logistics centres in Kyiv". A five-storey residential building in the city's Solomianskyi district was damaged by falling debris and a fire broke out. Rescue workers evacuated 35 people from the upper floors and two people died, with eight reported injured, including two children, according to Ukraine's state emergency service. In the Darnytskyi district of Kyiv, seven people were killed and another 14 injured after the attack caused fires and damage to houses, vehicles, an administrative and non-residential building, emergency services said. Elsewhere, emergency workers extinguished a fire in a non-residential building in the capital's Shevchenkivskyi district. Damage to commercial and residential buildings was reported in two other city districts. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has pressed the United States and other Western partners over Ukraine's need for more Patriot anti-ballistic missile defence systems to counter missile attacks from Russia. "Every package of ballistic missile interceptors saves the lives of our people. And every night without them results in more casualties," he wrote on X following the latest attacks. The Ukrainian leader late Friday said he spoke to US Vice-President JD Vance and discussed a meeting with President Donald Trump earlier this week in Washington, which Zelenskiy described as "positive and productive". "The Russian air strikes on our country continue and air defence, specifically interceptors for Patriot systems against ballistic missiles, remains a top priority," Zelenskiy said in a social media post. At a NATO summit in Ankara in July, Trump said the US would give Ukraine a license to make Patriot systems, but he appeared to move away from that commitment on Friday during a cabinet meeting at the presidential retreat in Camp David, Maryland, saying he had not yet made a final decision on the matter. From a basement shelter where she was taking cover as a second air alarm sounded for another wave, Liudmyla Nakonechna, 64, described how she was woken by loud explosions at 1.30am. "I ran into the corridor and was standing there when the bathroom door was blown off its hinges and struck me in the leg," said Nakonechna, whose health is poor after undergoing cancer treatment. "I heard the sound of shattering glass. My balcony was covered in glass and it was completely blown apart, while the windows in my bedroom were also blown out." Nakonechna had not taken cover in a shelter since Russia's full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022, but the stress became too much, she said. "It's getting worse by the day," Nakonechna said. "Whereas before there was an attack once every two weeks, or maybe once a week, now it happens practically every day. It is incredibly hard to bear this psychologically." Lithuania's foreign minister said the country's embassy in Kyiv was damaged when missiles struck nearby overnight. In Russian-occupied Crimea, the Moscow-appointed head of the city of Sevastopol, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said on Saturday that a 60-year-old woman was killed and two other people wounded in a drone attack on the city. http://www.russiaherald.com/news/2793343.text: Poland eyes spending up to $4.4 billion on Fort Trump RT.com 27 Sep 2026, 05:32 GMT+10 The project could be approved by the end of the year, according to Deputy Defense Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka Poland could pay up to 17 billion zloty ($4.4 billion) for a permanent base on its territory, the presidential National Security Bureau (BBN) has said. The project, which is currently being discussed with Washington, involves a facility that could house 5,000 troops, the agency told the newspaper Rzeczpospolita this week. Warsaw offered to host a permanent US base during President Donald Trump's first term in 2018, proposing to name the facility 'Fort Trump.' Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski confirmed this week that a deal on the base was nearing completion. Deputy Defense Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who traveled to the US this week for the talks on the base among other things, stated that the final decision rests with Trump and that she did not expect it to be made before the review of the posture of US forces, which is expected to be finalized in November or December. According to the BBN, the base could be completed in 2029 under "optimal conditions." Under Trump, Washington has pressed European NATO members to boost defense spending and take on more responsibility for arming Ukraine while the US concentrates resources on competing with China. The US is also widely expected to scale back its military presence in Europe as part of this strategy shift. America still considers Poland a "model ally," according to US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby, the man behind the US policy shift that has since become known as 'NATO 3.0.' Sobkowiak-Czarnecka also told journalists this week she had heard "many warm words from the American side acknowledging our preparedness and motivation." The US already has a permanent Army garrison and command headquarters in the city of Poznan, although most of the 10,000 US troops stationed in the country serve on a rotational basis. According to Deputy Defense Minister Stanislaw Wziatek, this number could grow to 15,000, with 5,000 stationed permanently at the new base. Warsaw has been one of Kiev's most ardent supporters in its ongoing conflict with Moscow. It also serves as a key logistics hub for delivering Western military aid to Ukraine while also bordering the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad to the northeast. Tensions between Moscow and Warsaw recently flared as Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski vowed to inflict a swift defeat upon Russia in case of a direct clash with NATO. "If Russia attacked us and we took our gloves off, I think we would defeat Russia quite quickly," he stated in mid-September, prompting Nikolay Patrushev, an aide to Russian President Vladimir Putin, to warn that Poland could "cease to exist" within days if it undertakes military action against Russia and forces Moscow to use its full arsenal. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmje.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, A shop also had its roof torn off in Milton, Florida By Madeline Halpert Reporting from New York Published 1 hour ago Four people have died and hundreds of thousands are without power after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern US with powerful winds and heavy rain. Officials reported two deaths each in the states of Alabama and Florida, which included people who were killed when trees fell on their houses. At least 600,000 people were without power in several states as of Saturday afternoon, according to tracker PowerOutage. Isaias made landfall in Florida late on Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105mph (168km/h) before being downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone. The storm felled trees and ripped the roofs off buildings. Alabama, Florida and Georgia all declared states of emergency ahead of its arrival, while both Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders to thousands of people. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The roof was blown off an apartment complex in Milton, Florida Image source, Getty Images Two deaths were reported in Florida's Escambia County. A woman was killed when a tree fell on her house, local Sheriff Chip Simmons said. Joey Williams told NewsNation his wife had died in the storm. He said they went outside to snap pictures of the damage but, when they went back into their home, a tree fell through the roof and trapped them. "I was able to squeeze out. My wife didn't make it," Williams told the outlet. Simmons later reported that a man had died from carbon monoxide poisoning after running a generator in a garage that was not properly ventilated. Four other people who were in the same house were taken to hospital. Officials had to rescue people in vehicles that became submerged by floodwaters. The Florida National Guard shared pictures of a truck stuck in a flood ditch, saying soldiers "stopped, swam to the vehicle and pulled its occupants to safety". Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said flooding was a continued risk and warned of a "very hazardous situation". Image source, EPA Image caption, In Florida, the storm tore through houses Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The canopy of a petrol station collapsed in Gulf Breeze, Florida In neighbouring Alabama, a sheriff was injured when a tree fell on him as he was responding to a car crash. "Unfortunately, we have also learned that two Alabamians have lost their lives," Governor Kay Ivey said in a post on X, without giving further details on the circumstances of the deaths. She also said officials were concerned about "spinoff tornadoes" in the state from the strong winds and heavy rain. "As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop," she said. In Charleston, South Carolina, officials asked people to stay home on Saturday night as high tide is expected to reach 7.5ft (2.3m). "After dark, floodwater is much harder to see and it's impossible to judge how deep it is from behind the wheel," the city said. The storm is expected to continue to weaken as it travels to the north-east, but the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) warned that the Carolinas and Georgia could see floods from up to 10 inches (25cm) of rainfall. In addition to Isaias, Tropical Storm Rachel is expected to hit southern California later on Saturday, and Hurricane Simon will hit the Pacific coast of Mexico on Sunday. Hurricane Isaias was the first hurricane in the Atlantic's hurricane season, which largely has been delayed due to El NiÃ±o conditions in the Pacific. https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/nauseda.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.10.16 10:16 Nausėda backs Ireland’s proposal to cut EU budget but criticises cuts to military mobility funding Translated by Karolis Broga Source: ELTA Gitanas Nausėda PHOTO: Dainius Labutis | Elta Follow Delfi on Google President Gitanas Nausėda supports a proposal by Ireland to cut the EU’s 2028–2034 budget by EUR 141 billion, but criticises proposed funding cuts for military mobility and competitiveness. „The EU’s financial framework is a very important document for me. I support the proposal put forward by Ireland, which currently holds the EU Council presidency – it is well-balanced. I am pleased that funding for cohesion and the Common Agricultural Policy is being maintained. Support for Ukraine also remains untouched,“ Nausėda told reporters in Brussels ahead of a European Council meeting. However, the president said he was unhappy with the proposed cuts to the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF), particularly funding for military mobility. He also expressed concern about reduced funding for the Competitiveness Fund and other funds. „We must understand that this budget has to be ambitious and its size is extremely important. The budget should remain close to the European Commission’s (EC) original proposal, and if we continue cutting spending during these lengthy discussions, we will lose sight of our priorities,“ the president said. Asked how he intended to persuade countries such as Germany not to make excessive cuts to the EU budget, Nausėda said he would do so through discussions. He also stressed that Lithuania would seek to maintain a common position with other countries supporting cohesion policy. „We have new priorities, but we also want to preserve our existing priorities, such as cohesion, competitiveness and the Common Agricultural Policy. We cannot keep the budget at the same level as in previous financial frameworks and say that we will also be able to address all the new priorities at the same time. That is economically, financially and mathematically impossible,“ the president said. Nausėda hopes an agreement on the new EU budget can be reached by the end of this year, although he acknowledged that negotiations would be difficult. He said Lithuania was ready to take an active part in the talks and was preparing to assume the presidency of the Council of the EU in the first half of next year. As previously reported, the EC’s original proposal for the EU’s 2028–2034 multiannual budget exceeds EUR 2 trillion, equivalent to around 1.26 percent of the bloc’s gross national income (GNI). Meanwhile, the European Parliament is calling for a larger budget in its negotiating position, equivalent to around 1.27 percent of GNI, excluding the cost of repaying loans under the EU’s recovery fund. All 27 EU member states will have to agree unanimously on the final multiannual budget. The agreement will also require the European Parliament’s approval.
